key_findings: Oxlint framework loading and oxfmt external formatting are fixed source-level extension lists, not custom parser/plugin hooks.
Vite+ resolves installed oxlint/oxfmt binaries and deliberately skips user Vite plugins for lint/format, making project-owned drop-in binaries the practical command integration seam.
Current oxc-vscode supports custom binary paths but omits .tsrx/ripple selectors and activation events, so a thin companion/client change is required.

Yuku packed TSRX parsing measured 136.74 MiB/s median versus 4.92 MiB/s for incumbent Acorn on the same valid Markless corpus; current OXC raw-transfer full TS AST measured 127.20 MiB/s, showing the native/data-oriented target is realistic.
Current TSRX Prettier measured 1.66 MiB/s and crashes on a valid BigInt Markless fixture; native oxfmt TS measured 37.39 MiB/s sequential and 315.91 MiB/s batched.
recommended_architecture: Pin OXC 0.140.0/source SHA 129b759131ec60294bfcc0f388a45264c8740507 and implement TSRX as a native source type with arena AST nodes, generated visitors, semantic traversal, oxlint and oxfmt CLI/LSP paths, drop-in Vite+ package resolution, and a thin ripple-language editor selector client. Use Ripple/Yuku/Prettier only as read-only grammar, differential, and behavior oracles.
